newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-UK stocks hit record on rate rise, stg falls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-UK stocks hit record on rate rise, stg falls.

text.p: British shares scaled new heights on Thursday as financial markets decided a new rise in Bank of England interest rates was probably the last one for now.
Government bond prices also surged but the pound was robbed of its support of higher interest rate prospects.
Sterling tumbled nearly five pfennigs, falling below three marks to hit a low of 2.9640 before steadying at 2.9664.

The Bank of England, given the authority to set interest rates shortly after the Labour government took office in early May, raised interest rates for the fourth time in as many months, taking official rates up a quarter point to seven percent.
The Bank's new Monetary Policy Committee hinted strongly in its statement accompanying the rate move that interest rates may now be close to peaking.
That was good news for beleaguered British exporters rendered increasingly uncompetitive by a rise of nearly 25 percent in the value of the pound over the last year.
The Bank acknowledged that the strong pound was putting "severe pressure" on British business, but said sterling's rise was linked to factors beyond its control.
Markets were heartened by news the Bank seemed to believe interest rates were now high enough to get the underlying rate of inflation below the government's target of 2-1/2 percent.
"Upward pressures on the exchange rate should be reduced by the perception that interest rates have reached a level consistent with the inflation target," the Committee said.
"The message is clear that that's it for now and it is highly unlikely rates will go up again September," said Ian Stewart, UK economist with Merrill Lynch.
It was a message the markets liked, twinning expectations that rates had peaked with hopes that there was no more bad news round the corner for companies from the currency side.
The FTSE index of 100 top British stock hit a new record of 5,095.3 in afternoon trade, before closing at 5,086.8, a rise of 1.21 percent or 60.6 points on the day.

Interest rate sensitive bank stocks were among the biggest gainers, with Barclays closing 114-1/2 pence higher at 1,442, benefiting additionally from an announcement of higher profits and news of plans to buy back more of its own shares.
Buyers were also active on the government bond market, with the key September Gilts contract rising 1/2 point to 115-05.
Ciaran Barr, an economist with Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said it was important to note that the Bank of England thought rates were now high enough to keep inflation in check.
"That is a clear signal that the Bank thinks it has done enough for the time being and it believes the move should put downward pressure on sterling," Barr said.
Barr said no further rate rise was now expected until November.
